title: On-prem audit proxy and customer blobstore integration
creator: Miguel Santos
description:
Goal: Build an on-prem / VPC-safe audit forwarding proxy that allows private deployments to reliably forward audit events to customer-managed blob stores (S3/GCS/Azure Blob) with strong authenticity, encryption-at-rest under customer keys, configurable retention, and operational observability. This ticket scopes the proxy design, auth modes, durability/ordering guarantees, backpressure handling, and integration patterns for customer-provided storage credentials and KMS/HSM wrapping.

Scope and non-goals:
- In scope: relay component running inside customer Private control plane that batches and uploads audit records, supports presigned/HMAC/SAS integration with S3/GCS/Azure, optional envelope encryption with customer KMS, retention metadata, error/retry semantics, and per-tenant config in Redwood Console for Private/VPC.
- Out of scope: building a hosted storage offering, cross-region replication for customer stores, or long-term cold-archive lifecycle rules (customers manage lifecycle on their side).

Design overview:
1) Relay architecture: lightweight daemon (go) runs in the same VPC/air-gapped environment as runtime nodes and ingests audit stream via local gRPC endpoint. It writes events to a durable local write-ahead log (rotating files) before attempting uploads. Uploads happen in append-friendly objects (daily shard + monotonically increasing sequence) to reduce small-file explosion.

2) Auth modes supported:
   - Presigned URLs / SAS tokens: recommended for short-lived uploads. Relay fetches presigned PUT URLs from Redwood control plane or accepts customer-provided templates via Console.
   - HMAC credentials (access key / secret): Relay uses SDK with temporary STS-style tokens when available; customers can supply IAM role-to-role trust config for non-interactive ops.
   - Service Account JSON (GCS): Relay supports OAuth2 token exchange with short-lived service account tokens; tokens are cached and refreshed.

3) Envelope encryption and KMS integration:
   - Two options: customer-managed server-side encryption (SSE-S3/SSE-KMS) or client-side envelope encryption.
   - For customer KMS integration, Relay calls customer KMS via an outbound-only encrypted channel; for air-gapped installs where KMS is internal, Relay can call internal KMS endpoints. Keys and key IDs are stored only as metadata; customer provides unexportable key IDs or wrapped CEKs.

4) Ordering and durability guarantees:
   - Guarantee: at-least-once delivery of audit batches to customer store; within a shard file, events are ordered by local event timestamp plus sequence.
   - Relay ensures events are durable to disk prior to upload. If an upload fails, exponential backoff + jitter and a dead-letter store (local) exist for manual retrieval.

5) Backpressure and rate limiting:
   - Relay exposes per-tenant rate limit config and configurable batching windows (max bytes and max time). If local disk fills beyond threshold, Relay applies shedding policy: oldest-evict with alerting or stop ingestion depending on admin-config.

6) Observability and audit of the audit pipeline:
   - Control plane exposes per-tenant upload metrics (success/failure, latency, bytes, events), and a small signed hash manifest is uploaded alongside each shard for integrity verification. Relay emits telemetry to a local metrics sink; metrics can be forwarded to customer telemetry endpoints.

7) Console UX/integration:
   - New Console flow: "Audit Forwarding > Destination" where users can add customer storage endpoints (S3/GCS/Azure), choose auth mode, select encryption (SSE-KMS or envelope), set retention metadata, and run test uploads. For Private, control plane stores only metadata and presigned token templates — never customer raw secrets unless explicitly requested for managed installs.

Security considerations and threat model:
- Sensitive secrets: avoid long-lived credentials; prefer short-lived presigned URLs or token exchange. If credentials must be stored for managed onboarding, insist on KMS-wrapped secrets and strict RBAC.
- Replay/forgery: include per-shard manifest signed by Relay private key; control plane provides a verification path.
- Privilege separation: Relay runs as non-root, uses filesystem ACLs for WAL, and signs uploads with ephemeral credentials.

Implementation plan (phases):
- Phase 1 (MVP): implement relay with S3 presigned PUT and HMAC support, local WAL, daily sharding, basic retry, and Console config page + test upload. Metrics exported to Prometheus. (owner: Asha)
- Phase 2: add GCS/Azure clients, client-side envelope encryption, KMS exchange hooks, improved manifest signing, DLQ tooling, and e2e QA in private staging.
- Phase 3: hardened RBAC, long-term retention policy UI, automatic anomaly alerts for failed uploads, and full enterprise security review.

Testing and rollout:
- Unit + integration tests for SDK calls, durability semantics, and backpressure. End-to-end test deploying the Relay into a private staging VPC with a mock S3 (minio) and a GCS emulator. Load test at peak audit rates (simulate 10k reqs/sec across tenants).
- Canary rollout: offer Relay as opt-in for a subset of Private customers; monitor DLQ size, upload success rates, and Console UX metrics before full rollout.

APIs and artifacts:
- control plane endpoints: POST /audit-destinations, GET /audit-destinations/{id}/test-upload, PATCH for rotation.
- console page: link to attachments and runbook.

Operational runbook highlights:
- How to rotate presigned templates and revoke a destination:
  1) Mark destination revoked in Console (control plane will stop issuing presigned URLs).
  2) Relay will stop attempting new uploads to that destination and retain local WAL for 30 days for retrieval.
- DLQ handling: provide tooling to download failed shards for offline replay.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Should we support append-to-object vs object-per-batch? Current design chooses object-per-batch with naming convention to avoid object size locking on some providers; append APIs (GCS compose) considered but adds complexity.
- How much secret material do we store in control plane for managed installs? We prefer metadata-only approach, but some onboarding flows may require temporary retention of wrapped credentials.

Acceptance criteria:
- Relay can successfully upload 99.9% of audit events to S3/GCS/Azure under normal conditions in staging.
- Console destination flow works end-to-end with test upload.
- Security review completed and remediation items tracked.

Related docs and links: see attachments for design spec, Confluence runbook, and draft PRs.
